title: The Clause at the Bottom of the Bond: Elliott, the Holdout, and the Ship at Tema
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Teaneck, the pharmacist's son
stops.date_confidence: attested; birthdate from Wikipedia, 'Paul Singer (businessman)', not corroborated against a registry
stops.campa: A son is born in Teaneck, on the Jersey side of the Hudson, to a Manhattan pharmacist and a homemaker, in a Jewish household of the ordinary postwar sort. They name him Paul Elliott. The middle name is chosen for its sound; thirty-three years later it will be painted on the door of a fund that sues countries and impounds their ships. Teaneck in 1944 is commuter country, twenty minutes from the George Washington Bridge, lawns and small pharmacies of exactly the kind his father keeps across the river.
suggested_refs: Teaneck, New Jersey, and the postwar Bergen County commuter belt

stops.name: Rochester, the psychology degree
stops.date_confidence: year attested, month conventional. Wikipedia gives a B.S. in psychology; other profiles have written B.A., and the research pool contradicted itself on the point. The registrar was not consulted.
stops.campa: Four years at the University of Rochester, and the degree he takes is in psychology: the study of what people do under pressure, and why. There is no economics in it, no accounting, nothing that points at a bond market. What the discipline does teach is how to read a counterparty across a table, which is not nothing in the trade he will eventually enter. He leaves upstate New York in the summer of 1966 with a science of motive and no trade at all. Rochester will hand him an honorary doctorate fifty-one years later.
suggested_refs: University of Rochester alumni records for the class of 1966

stops.name: Cambridge, Harvard Law School
stops.date_confidence: year attested, month conventional
stops.campa: He takes the J.D. at Harvard, three years inside the American common law of contract, and this is the education that turns out to matter. The instrument he becomes famous for is not a trade but a sentence: a line of boilerplate sitting unread near the bottom of a sovereign bond, saying only that the obligations shall rank equally among themselves. Lawyers had passed over pari passu for a century as decoration. He is being taught, in these rooms, to read the parts of a document that nobody reads.
suggested_refs: The pari passu clause in New York-law sovereign bond indentures

stops.name: New York, the real estate desk at Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette
stops.date_confidence: [R]: the employment is reconstruction in the sources reached, year given as 1974 by Wikipedia, month a default. The pin is DLJ's address at 140 Broadway, not documented as Singer's own desk.
stops.campa: He arrives on Wall Street as a lawyer rather than a trader, hired into the real estate division of Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette to paper other people's deals. It is the ordinary route in: an attorney at the edge of the room where the money is decided, watching the arithmetic get made by people with less schooling than he has. He never again practises law for anybody but himself. He stays roughly three years and then he is gone. Why he went, and what he made of the work, went unrecorded.
suggested_refs: Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette, 140 Broadway, in the 1970s

stops.name: Manhattan, Elliott Associates founded
stops.date_confidence: January 1977 and the $1.3 million are attested (Wikipedia, 'Elliott Investment Management'). The pin is Elliott's much later Midtown headquarters at 40 West 57th Street: the 1977 founding address is undocumented in every source reached, and a pool entry implying continuous occupation from 1977 is unsupported.
stops.campa: In January he opens a fund with one million three hundred thousand dollars raised from friends and from family, and names it after his own middle name. The first strategy is convertible arbitrage, dull and patient and hedged. It survives 1987 and it survives 2008 and it goes decades without a losing year. What begins here as a small book will end as tens of billions under management and a name finance ministers learn to pronounce. The street address of that first office is not recorded anywhere reachable.
suggested_refs: Elliott Associates L.P., founded January 1977; the firm's later headquarters at 40 West 57th Street

stops.name: Lima, the Banco de la Nacion paper
stops.date_confidence: contradiction not resolved: Wikipedia's 'Elliott Investment Management' dates the purchase 1995, its 'Paul Singer (businessman)' dates it 1996. Month is a default. The pool also mislabelled the instrument as Brady bonds; it was unrestructured bank loan paper.
stops.campa: Peru has been in default on its commercial bank loans since the crisis years of the eighties, and the banks that made them have written them down and want out. A discounted loan is a bet on repayment; an unrestructured loan is a bet on a courtroom. Elliott buys roughly twenty million dollars of face value for eleven million four hundred thousand, and then does what no buyer of dead paper is expected to do: it refuses the Brady exchange that every other creditor accepts, and keeps the original claim whole.
stops.quote: a pioneer in the business of buying up sovereign bonds on the cheap, and then going after countries for unpaid debts
stops.quote_source: The Independent on Paul Singer, as quoted in Wikipedia, 'Paul Singer (businessman)'; the original article was not accessed
suggested_refs: Elliott Associates LP v. Banco de la Nacion, the Peruvian bank-debt litigation

stops.name: Manhattan, the judgment against Peru
stops.date_confidence: year attested (Wikipedia, 'Elliott Investment Management'), month a default. The research pool had collapsed purchase, judgment and collection into a single 1996 entry.
stops.campa: A New York court awards Elliott the full face of the loans plus past due interest: fifty-eight million dollars against eleven million four hundred thousand paid. On paper this is total victory, and in practice it is a piece of paper. A sovereign that does not wish to satisfy a judgment simply does not satisfy it, and the property of a state abroad is wrapped in immunities designed precisely to prevent what Elliott now intends. The question is no longer whether Peru owes the money. It is where on earth Peru can be touched.
suggested_refs: Elliott Associates LP v. Banco de la Nacion, S.D.N.Y., 1998 judgment

stops.name: Brussels, the Euroclear injunction
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the Brussels Court of Appeal ruling; described secondhand, the ruling itself was not accessed
stops.campa: The answer is Belgium. Peru's payments to its restructured creditors clear through Euroclear in Brussels, and Elliott persuades the Brussels Court of Appeal to freeze that settlement unless Elliott is paid alongside them. The effect is surgical: Peru can now pay everyone, or nobody. The pari passu doctrine is not yet in this, only the instinct behind it, which is to find the pipe through which a country pays and put a hand on it. Within weeks the treasury pays in full rather than fall back into default over a debt it had thought long buried.
suggested_refs: The Euroclear settlement system, Brussels, and the September 2000 injunction
sources: Brussels Court of Appeal ruling of 26 September 2000, as reported in the financial and legal press

stops.name: Lima, Fujimori's aircraft
stops.date_confidence: [R] tradition. The research pool tags this reconstruction and gives no year within Fujimori's flight; November 2000 is placed to match the flight itself. No primary source was reached and the episode may be legend.
stops.campa: In the same season Alberto Fujimori's government comes apart in the corruption tapes and the president leaves for Japan. The story that attaches itself to Elliott, and that Singer has never publicly denied, is that the firm had his aircraft confiscated and offered him passage in exchange for the treasury settling the fifty-eight million. Folklore runs some years ahead of doctrine here. The tale is told everywhere and sourced nowhere: no filing, no date, no name of an airfield, and no reporter who has produced one.
suggested_refs: Alberto Fujimori's flight to Japan and resignation by fax, November 2000
sources: Wikipedia, 'Paul Singer (businessman)' (tagged [R] in the research pool, no primary citation)

stops.name: Brazzaville, the Congo paper
stops.date_confidence: contradiction not resolved: the pool's chronology dated the purchase 1998, its own afterlife lens dated the campaign to the 2000s, and the English judgments of 2002-2003 favour the later reading. c. 2001 is used, month a default.
stops.campa: The Republic of Congo has defaulted on commercial loans through decades of civil war and oil revenue that leaves the country by routes nobody publishes. A Cayman vehicle called Kensington International, owned by Elliott, buys thirty-two point six million dollars of that debt for under twenty million. The oil is the reason. Congolese crude is sold through traders and shipped to refineries in Europe and America, and every cargo is a moment when the property of a sovereign becomes visible inside a jurisdiction that has courts.
suggested_refs: Kensington International Ltd., the Elliott vehicle for the Congo position

stops.name: London, the Royal Courts of Justice
stops.date_confidence: the English High Court judgments run 2002 to 2003; no single date was verified and the month is a default. The judgments themselves were not accessed.
stops.campa: The English High Court gives Kensington judgment against the Republic of Congo for more than a hundred million dollars, and the judgments are only the start of what is done with them. Disclosure in the English proceedings drags into daylight the offshore structures through which Congolese oil is sold, with the names of officials standing on both sides of the sale. No campaign against corruption in Brazzaville had ever obtained that record. A creditor chasing its own money obtains it in the course of the chase. The transcripts are public and stay public.
suggested_refs: Kensington International Ltd v Republic of Congo, English High Court, 2002-2003
sources: UK court reporting on Kensington International v Republic of Congo

stops.name: Brazzaville, the settlement and the unlikely ally
stops.date_confidence: year attested, month a default. The figure of roughly ninety million dollars comes from later reporting relayed by Wikipedia without a citation and is soft; the settlement sum was never published.
stops.campa: After years of asset chases across several jurisdictions the Congo litigation ends in a settlement whose figure is never published, put since at somewhere near ninety million dollars. Congolese campaigners against corruption find themselves crediting a distressed debt fund out of Manhattan for evidence they could not get any other way. Nobody designed that and Elliott had not sought it. What is left behind in the court files is a public record of how the country's oil money actually moves.
stops.quote: we would not know any facts about the way our country's wealth is being taken away
stops.quote_source: Brice Mackosso, Congolese anti-corruption campaigner, saying that if it were not for funds like Elliott 'we would not know any facts about the way our country's wealth is being taken away'; Lydia Polgreen, 'Unlikely Ally Against Congo Republic Graft', New York Times, 10 December 2007. Verified at the Wikipedia layer only, the NYT being unreachable from this host.
suggested_refs: Lydia Polgreen, 'Unlikely Ally Against Congo Republic Graft', New York Times, 10 December 2007

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the largest default in the world
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The amount is corrected from the pool's 'roughly $100 billion' to the US$93 billion of external debt, about $81.8 billion of it in bonds, given by Wikipedia, 'Argentine debt restructuring'.
stops.campa: Four presidents in eleven days, the banks shuttered under the corralito, the peso about to lose two thirds of itself, and on the twenty-sixth of December the Republic stops paying ninety-three billion dollars of external debt, some eighty-two billion of it in bonds. It is the largest sovereign default there has ever been. The bonds themselves do not vanish. They go on trading at twenty cents, then fifteen, then a handful, passing out of the hands of pension funds and into the hands of people who buy broken things on purpose.
suggested_refs: The Argentine default of 26 December 2001 and the corralito

stops.name: Manhattan, NML Capital takes the position
stops.date_confidence: the purchases are attested as beginning after the December 2001 default; no month is given in any source reached, and this date stands for a position accumulated across years
stops.campa: Elliott buys through NML Capital Limited, a Cayman Islands affiliate whose name will end up better known in Buenos Aires than the fund's own. The instrument that turns a distressed purchase into a claim on a state is not a trade but a sentence in the contract, and the work of it will run fifteen years. The two figures reported later are the whole arithmetic the word vulture is about: forty-nine million dollars paid on the secondary market, against a claim of eight hundred and thirty-two million by 2014.
stops.quote: one of the smartest and toughest money managers in the business
stops.quote_source: Fortune, 2012, on Paul Singer, as quoted in Wikipedia, 'Paul Singer (businessman)'; the original was not accessed
suggested_refs: NML Capital Ltd., Cayman Islands affiliate of Elliott Management

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the first exchange refused
stops.date_confidence: the first exchange ran January to February 2005; the date given is the opening of the offer, and the 25 to 30 cents figure is the pool's approximation
stops.campa: Argentina offers its creditors an exchange at roughly twenty-five to thirty cents on the dollar, take it or hold paper worth nothing. Some seventy-six percent of bondholders take it. NML Capital does not, and neither do a scattering of others, most of them funds that bought after the default with litigation already in view. Holding out is not a protest. It is a position: the exchange creditors have converted their claim into something Argentina means to service, and the holdouts still own the original promise, entire, with interest running.
suggested_refs: The 2005 Argentine debt exchange and the holdout creditors

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the second exchange and the lock
stops.date_confidence: the second exchange ran April to June 2010; the date given is approximate to its opening. The Lock Law (Ley Cerrojo) was passed in 2005 and suspended for the 2010 exchange, then restored.
stops.campa: A second exchange lifts acceptance to about ninety-three percent, and Argentina keeps on its books a Lock Law forbidding its own government from ever offering the holdouts better terms. The statute is meant to prove the offer final. It also removes any lawful route by which Argentina could settle, which turns a negotiation into a siege that only a repeal or a court can end. Seven percent of the debt now stands outside the restructuring, and NML Capital holds a piece of it large enough to matter.
suggested_refs: The Ley Cerrojo (Lock Law) and the 2010 Argentine exchange

stops.name: London, the United Kingdom Supreme Court
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day, NML Capital Ltd v Republic of Argentina [2011] UKSC 31, case UKSC 2010/0040, Lords Phillips, Walker, Mance, Collins and Clarke. The research pool gave 29 June 2011, wrong by a week, with a pin about 150 m east of the building.
stops.campa: The lower English courts had held Argentina immune from enforcement in Britain. Five judges sitting in the old Middlesex Guildhall on Parliament Square hold otherwise, and NML Capital may pursue Argentine assets in the United Kingdom. It is a narrow ruling about state immunity and a very wide one about geography. From here the search runs wherever Argentina keeps anything at all, and before the Republic moves money or sends a ship out it has to ask whose courts it is entering.
suggested_refs: NML Capital Ltd v Republic of Argentina [2011] UKSC 31

stops.name: Manhattan, Griesa reads the clause
stops.date_confidence: attested 23 February 2012 for the pari passu holding. The research pool dated this 2012-11, which belongs to the amended injunction operationalizing the holding after the Second Circuit's 26 October 2012 remand; the two judicial acts are distinct and the pool conflated them.
stops.campa: In the Southern District of New York, Judge Thomas Griesa accepts the reading Elliott's lawyers have pressed for years. The pari passu clause in the bonds, the boilerplate saying the obligations rank equally, means that Argentina may not pay the exchange bondholders unless it pays the holdouts ratably at the same moment. A century of contracts had carried that sentence as ornament. In a few paragraphs it becomes a lever long enough to halt the payments of a state. The order issues on the twenty-third of February.
stops.quote: we've made the point over and over again that sovereigns that could pay their debts and choose not to may be attempting to save some money but are harming their people and their economies by making investing in their countries more risky and more problematic and by discouraging foreign investment
stops.quote_source: Paul Singer to Alpha Magazine, 2013, as reported in Jaime Fuller, 'Meet the wealthy donor who's trying to get Republicans to support gay marriage', Washington Post, 4 April 2014. Both originals unreachable from this host (the Post returned HTTP 403); verified at the Wikipedia layer only.
suggested_refs: NML Capital, Ltd. v. Republic of Argentina, S.D.N.Y., the pari passu holding of 23 February 2012

stops.name: Foley Square, the Second Circuit affirms
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the opinion itself was not accessed
stops.campa: The Court of Appeals upholds Griesa's interpretation and returns the case only for the mechanics of the injunction. Argentina's argument, that no court may order a sovereign how to allocate its payments, loses. Commentators start calling this the sovereign debt trial of the century. In London and in Frankfurt, lawyers pull old prospectuses off their shelves to see what else their clients have been signing since the nineteen seventies without reading it, and the answer, in most cases, is the same sentence.
suggested_refs: NML Capital, Ltd. v. Republic of Argentina, 2d Cir., 26 October 2012

stops.name: Foley Square, affirmed a second time
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: The amended injunction comes back on appeal and is affirmed. Argentina's alternative, a voluntary plan to pay the holdouts on terms of its own choosing, is dismissed; the court has no interest in an offer the plaintiffs have already refused. Cristina Fernández de Kirchner says from Buenos Aires that Argentina will not pay the vultures, and she means it exactly. Everything now turns on whether four justices of the Supreme Court will vote to hear it.
suggested_refs: NML Capital, Ltd. v. Republic of Argentina, 2d Cir., 23 August 2013

stops.name: Washington, the Court declines
stops.date_confidence: certiorari denied June 2014; the day is as commonly reported and was not verified against the order list
stops.campa: The Supreme Court refuses to take the appeal, without comment, which leaves the Second Circuit's reading of pari passu standing as law in the jurisdiction where nearly every sovereign bond on earth is written. Justice Samuel Alito, who six years earlier flew to an Alaskan fishing lodge on Singer's aircraft, does not recuse himself. As law the case is finished; what remains is enforcement, aimed at a country that has already said it will default again rather than comply. No opinion accompanies the denial, and none is required of them.
stops.quote: a fight against charlatans who refuse to play by the market's rules
stops.quote_source: Paul Singer, quoted in Bloomberg, 7 August 2014, as cited in Wikipedia, 'Paul Singer (businessman)'; the original was not accessed
suggested_refs: Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd., certiorari denied June 2014
ProPublica reporting on Justice Alito's undisclosed travel

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the technical default
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: Argentina wires the interest due on the restructured bonds and the injunction stops the money at the trustee, since nothing may go out unless the holdouts are paid too. A country that has serviced its debt for nine years is in default because a New York court has decided that a sentence in the contract means what nobody thought it meant. The rating agencies call it selective default. Argentina insists it has paid, and puts about a word of its own for what has been done to it instead: griefault, after the name of the judge.
stops.quote: Nobody can predict how long governments can get away with fake growth, fake money, fake jobs, fake financial stability, fake inflation numbers and fake income growth.
stops.quote_source: Elliott Management investor letter, November 2014, as quoted in Wikipedia, 'Elliott Investment Management'; the letter itself was not accessed
suggested_refs: The Argentine selective default of 30 July 2014

stops.name: Tema, the ARA Libertad detained
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The pool's 'roughly 200 cadets stranded for weeks' is corrected: about 300 were aboard, most repatriated within days, roughly 45 remaining with the ship. She is a full-rigged sail training vessel; the Argentine Navy's 'fragata' misleads as 'frigate' in English.
stops.campa: The Argentine navy's sail training ship, a three-masted steel square-rigger on a goodwill cruise, ties up at the Ghanaian port of Tema and is not permitted to leave. NML Capital's local counsel has obtained an order from a Ghanaian court attaching her as security for the judgment. Some three hundred people are aboard, most of them cadets; the great majority fly home within days and about forty-five stay with the ship. Her captain refuses to let anyone board, and the standoff at the quay runs on for ten weeks.
suggested_refs: ARA Libertad (Q-2), detained at Tema, October to December 2012
The High Court of Ghana at Accra, attachment order of October 2012
sources: Contemporaneous BBC and Reuters reporting, October to December 2012

stops.name: Hamburg, the tribunal orders her released
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day, ITLOS Case No. 20. Coordinates corrected: the research pool gave three different pins for this building, one of them about 9 km out in the Altstadt; the tribunal gives its own position as 53 degrees 33 minutes 04 seconds north, 9 degrees 51 minutes 03 seconds east.
stops.campa: Argentina takes Ghana, not Elliott, before the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea in the villa quarter of Nienstedten above the Elbe, and wins unanimously. A warship is immune from civil process, and a naval training vessel is a warship; no commercial dispute reaches her hull. It is the clearest defeat the strategy suffers in any court anywhere. Ghana releases her on the nineteenth of December and she sails for home, reaching Mar del Plata on the ninth of January with a crowd waiting on the quay.
stops.quote: forthwith and unconditionally release the frigate ARA Libertad
stops.quote_source: International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea, ARA Libertad (Argentina v. Ghana), Case No. 20, Order of 15 December 2012
suggested_refs: ITLOS Case No. 20, ARA Libertad (Argentina v. Ghana), Order of 15 December 2012

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the word buitre
stops.date_confidence: the pool's quote lens places these remarks at Buenos Aires without a date; its own gap note ties the 'depredadores sociales globales' line to 9 January 2013, the day the Libertad reached Mar del Plata. The canonical Buenos Aires pin is kept and the disagreement is recorded rather than resolved. The speech was not independently verified.
stops.campa: Cristina Fernández de Kirchner has spent years giving the fight its vocabulary, and the vocabulary outlasts every ruling. Fondos buitre: vulture funds, the birds that circle what is already dying. It travels from her podium into the Spanish press, then the Italian and the French, and at last into English, where Singer carries it for the rest of his career and objects to it in interviews. He is not the first investor to buy defaulted sovereign paper and sue. He is the one who got named.
stops.quote: los buitres son las aves que comienzan a volar sobre los muertos; los fondos buitre sobrevuelan sobre países endeudados y en default. Son depredadores sociales globales.
stops.quote_source: Cristina Fernández de Kirchner on the fondos buitre, quoted in Spanish Wikipedia, 'Fondos buitre'; the original speech was not independently verified
suggested_refs: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Fondos buitre'
The Argentine government's 'Argentina paga' campaign against the holdout creditors

stops.name: Manhattan, the mediator's room
stops.date_confidence: attested for 29 February 2016 and for Daniel Pollack's role as special master. The exact Manhattan office is not independently confirmed and the pin is approximate; the research pool wrongly placed this event at the Casa Rosada in Buenos Aires.
stops.campa: Mauricio Macri has been president for eleven weeks and campaigned on ending this. In a New York law office the court-appointed special master Daniel Pollack runs marathon sessions between Argentine officials and the holdouts, Singer's NML Capital foremost among them, and on the twenty-ninth of February an agreement in principle is reached. Three numbers circulate afterwards and they are not the same quantity: four point six five billion to the four lead holdouts, six and a half billion in Argentina's broader February offer, and about two point four billion to Elliott alone.
suggested_refs: Daniel Pollack, special master in NML Capital v. Republic of Argentina
Financial Times reporting on the February 2016 agreement in principle

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the Congress repeals the lock
stops.date_confidence: the repeal passed the Chamber of Deputies in mid March 2016 and the Senate on 31 March; the later date is used. Canonical Palacio del Congreso pin inherited from javier_milei.journey.json.
stops.campa: Nothing can be paid until the laws forbidding payment are gone. In the Palacio del Congreso the deputies and then the senators debate through the night and strike out the Lock Law and the Sovereign Payment Law, the two statutes by which the previous government had bound its successors to refuse. A sovereign has to unmake its own legislation before a New York injunction will come off. The Kirchnerist blocs vote against and call the settlement a capitulation to a foreign creditor. The repeal carries.
suggested_refs: The repeal of the Ley Cerrojo and the Ley de Pago Soberano, March 2016

stops.name: Manhattan, the injunctions lift
stops.date_confidence: sequence corrected: Griesa ordered the injunctions vacated 19 February 2016 conditional on repeal and payment, the Second Circuit affirmed that vacatur 13 April 2016, and the injunctions lifted on payment 22 April 2016. The research pool assigned the April action to Griesa's court.
stops.campa: Argentina raises sixteen and a half billion dollars in a single sale, the largest emerging-market bond issue on record, and pays. The injunctions come off, the docket closes, and the country is back in the credit markets it walked out of in 2001. Elliott's return on the Argentine position gets reported in multiples rather than percentages. Fifteen years of litigation end with a government working out that paying costs less than being locked out. Nothing in the settlement disturbs the doctrine. It stands where the Second Circuit left it.
suggested_refs: Argentina's April 2016 bond issue and the payment to the holdout creditors

stops.name: Troy, the Delphi bankruptcy
stops.date_confidence: year attested, month a default. Coordinates corrected: the pool's pin fell about 3 km south of 5725 Delphi Drive. Delphi Holdings was acquired jointly by Elliott and Silver Point Capital (Wikipedia, 'Aptiv'); the $12.9 billion originates in a 2012 Nation investigation as an aggregate of Treasury outlays connected to Delphi, not as a sum paid to Elliott, which is how the pool stated it.
stops.campa: General Motors spun its parts division out in 1999 and it fails in the crash along with everything else in Michigan. Elliott and Silver Point Capital, holding senior debt, take the company through bankruptcy and out the far side while the federal auto rescue is paying to keep the industry breathing. Critics later add up every Treasury outlay connected to Delphi into one figure, twelve point nine billion dollars, and present it as the fund's take. It was never a payment to Elliott. The pensions the Delphi salaried retirees lost were real.
stops.quote: It's true that monetary policy was too lax for too long, and the government encouraged lending to people who were unlikely to repay their loans. But this crisis was primarily caused by managements and individuals throughout the financial system who exercised extremely poor judgement. The private sector, not the public sector, is where the biggest mistakes were made.
stops.quote_source: Paul Singer, Wall Street Journal opinion column, 2009, as quoted in Wikipedia, 'Paul Singer (businessman)'; the column was not accessed
suggested_refs: Delphi Holdings LLP and the 2009 auto bailout
The Nation investigation of 2012 into Treasury outlays connected to Delphi

stops.name: Hawthorne, the satellite contract
stops.date_confidence: March 2014 attested for the filing, day not given. The suit was filed in US federal court in New York against a California company; the pin is the defendant's headquarters rather than the courthouse.
stops.campa: NML's lawyers go looking for Argentine property anywhere inside American commerce and turn up a contract: the Argentine space agency has paid a rocket company in Hawthorne, California to put two communications satellites into orbit, something like a hundred and thirteen million dollars of it. The fund sues SpaceX to attach the money. The method behind the suit treats every dollar a sovereign spends abroad as a place the sovereign can be found. The suit fails. The satellites launch on schedule.
suggested_refs: NML Capital's 2014 attachment suit against SpaceX over ARSAT launch payments

stops.name: Seoul, against the Samsung merger
stops.date_confidence: the shareholder vote on the Samsung C&T / Cheil Industries merger was held 17 July 2015
stops.campa: Elliott holds a stake in Samsung C&T and fights the merger with Cheil Industries that will consolidate the Lee family's control of the whole group. The argument is the ordinary activist one, that the exchange ratio robs the minority. Elliott loses the shareholder vote when the National Pension Service, voting the retirement savings of the country, sides with the family. Two years later Lee Jae-yong is convicted of bribery connected to obtaining that same vote. The merger is not undone.
suggested_refs: The 2015 Samsung C&T and Cheil Industries merger vote
The bribery conviction of Lee Jae-yong

stops.name: Seoul, the vulture on the corporate website
stops.date_confidence: year attested; no month is given in any source reached, and September is a placeholder within the merger dispute
stops.campa: During the same fight a Samsung company website publishes cartoons in which a hook-nosed vulture in a business suit picks at Korean firms. Singer is not named in them and does not need to be. The bird had been Argentina's word for him first, and a Korean conglomerate borrows it for a proxy fight. The images run for some days before they are pulled down and disowned by Samsung as antisemitic caricature. Who chose the figure, and what they took themselves to be drawing, never came out.
suggested_refs: The Samsung cartoons of 2015 and their withdrawal
sources: 2015 press coverage of the Samsung and Elliott dispute

stops.name: Milan, the club that came with the loan
stops.date_confidence: July 2018 attested for the transfer of ownership; the day is as commonly reported
stops.campa: Elliott had lent Li Yonghong the money to buy AC Milan and taken the club as collateral. He defaults, and the fund finds itself holding seven European Cups, a half share of the San Siro, and a support that has never heard of distressed debt and learns the name of an American hedge fund in a weekend. Elliott recapitalizes, installs management, wins a league title in 2022 and sells in the same year at roughly three times what it put in. Nobody in Manhattan had set out to buy a football club.
suggested_refs: Elliott Management's ownership of AC Milan, 2018 to 2022

stops.name: San Francisco, the stake in Twitter
stops.date_confidence: the stake was reported at the end of February 2020 and the settlement announced 9 March 2020; the day given is approximate to the disclosure
stops.campa: Elliott takes about two billion dollars of Twitter and moves to remove Jack Dorsey, who is running two public companies at once and talking about spending half the year in Africa. The usual sequence ends with the founder gone. This one does not: Dorsey keeps the job, Elliott takes board seats and a buyback, and a settlement is announced inside two weeks. Elliott's people stay on the board after the truce. Dorsey resigns twenty-one months later, at a time of his own choosing.
suggested_refs: Elliott Management's 2020 campaign at Twitter, Inc.

stops.name: Dallas, the airline
stops.date_confidence: the $1.9 billion stake was disclosed in June 2024. Gary Kelly was Executive Chairman, not chief executive, having been succeeded as CEO by Bob Jordan in February 2022, and his retirement was announced in September 2024; the research pool merged the two events and gave the wrong title.
stops.campa: Elliott discloses one point nine billion dollars of Southwest Airlines and demands that the leadership go. Southwest is the last big American carrier without assigned seats or bag fees, a company that built an identity out of doing it differently, and the fund's case is that the identity is costing the shareholders money. By September the executive chairman Gary Kelly announces his retirement and the board is reshuffled. Assigned seating is coming. The chief executive, Bob Jordan, keeps his job.

stops.name: Davos: "hedge funds are pretty opaque too"
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the exchange is widely quoted with this wording and attributed to the Financial Times, in the period of heightened scrutiny of bank risk disclosure following JPMorgan's 2012 London Whale loss, but this session could not independently re-verify the exact year or session against a live source; the World Economic Forum's annual January meeting is the setting in every account and 2013 is placed here as the best-supported year, not a confirmed one
stops.campa: At the World Economic Forum he needles the banks from the floor of critics: their published accounts are so opaque, he says, that no outsider can tell which of them are actually sound and which are quietly rotten. Jamie Dimon, on the panel, does not let it pass. With all due respect, he answers, hedge funds are pretty opaque too. The exchange gets repeated for years afterward as the neatest two lines in the whole argument over financial transparency, a vulture and a bank chief agreeing on nothing except that neither side can really see the other's books.
